item.content:encoded:
The Globe and Mail Foundation Scholarship for a Syrian Media Professional offers a unique opportunity for a Syrian media worker to receive advanced journalism training, professional mentorship and international reporting experience through the University of Toronto’s Dalla Lana Fellowship in Journalism and Health Impact.

The part-time fellowship is designed to help a Syrian media professional strengthen their journalism skills, develop stories for international audiences and build connections with global newsroom editors. The programme will run from September 8, 2026, to March 16, 2027, and participants can complete the programme entirely online from anywhere in the world.

About the Fellowship

The Globe and Mail Foundation is partnering with the University of Toronto’s Dalla Lana Fellowship in Journalism and Health Impact to support and train a Syrian media professional who wants to develop their career as a journalist working with Canadian and international media.

The fellowship focuses on helping subject-matter specialists and media professionals learn how to turn their areas of expertise into effective reporting beats.

Although the programme includes a strong health and journalism component, applicants are not limited to health-related specialties. The selected Fellow will have the opportunity to identify a reporting area that they want to develop and produce stories aimed at an international audience.

The programme is particularly intended to provide professional support to a Syrian media professional during Syria’s transition and help them build the skills and experience needed to engage with global journalism platforms.

What the Fellowship Provides

The selected Fellow will receive training, mentorship and practical experience in several areas of journalism.

Key areas include:

  • Journalism training for international reporting
  • Direct mentorship from programme faculty
  • Guidance in finding and developing story ideas
  • Support with pitching stories to editors
  • Training in investigative journalism
  • Training in AI for reporting
  • Guidance on developing and maintaining a freelance journalism practice
  • Career planning and professional development
  • Opportunities to engage with an international journalism audience
  • Additional support and mentorship from The Globe and Mail Foundation based on the Fellow’s needs

A major component of the programme is the opportunity for the Fellow to find, pitch and report their own stories. This allows participants to move beyond classroom learning and develop practical experience in producing journalism for a broader international audience.

Programme Format and Dates

The fellowship is a part-time programme running from:

September 8, 2026 – March 16, 2027

Participants do not have to relocate to Canada because the entire programme can be completed online.

In-person attendance is not required, making the opportunity accessible to the selected Fellow regardless of their location.

The programme consists of three main components:

1. Two-Week Journalism Bootcamp

The programme begins with an intensive two-week bootcamp running from:

September 8–18, 2026

The bootcamp provides the foundation for the fellowship and prepares participants for the subsequent training, reporting and mentorship activities.

2. Weekly Cohort Sessions

From September 22, 2026, to March 16, 2027, Fellows will participate in weekly full-cohort teaching and story meetings.

These sessions provide opportunities to learn alongside other participants, discuss story ideas and receive guidance on journalism projects.

3. Monthly Skills Classes

From October 2026 through March 2027, Fellows will participate in skills classes held on one Friday/Saturday pair each month.

These sessions will focus on practical journalism skills that participants can apply to their reporting and professional careers.

A Focus on International Journalism

One of the central objectives of the fellowship is to help the selected Syrian media professional develop the ability to work with global newsroom editors and international audiences.

The programme provides training in how to:

  • Identify strong international story ideas
  • Develop reporting beats
  • Research and investigate stories
  • Pitch stories effectively
  • Produce journalism for international media
  • Work with editors
  • Build a professional journalism portfolio
  • Develop a sustainable freelance practice

This makes the fellowship particularly valuable for a media professional who wants to expand beyond local or regional reporting and begin contributing to international media.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity is specifically designed for a Syrian media professional.

Applicants should:

  • Be a media professional from Syria
  • Have a good working knowledge of English
  • Have an interest in international journalism and reporting
  • Be able to participate in the part-time programme from September 2026 to March 2027
  • Be prepared to develop and pitch their own story ideas
  • Have an interest in developing a reporting beat for Canadian or international media

The source information does not specify a minimum academic qualification, age requirement or particular university degree.

Applicants who have previous reporting experience may submit up to three reporting clips, although this is optional. The clips may be submitted in Arabic.

APPLY HERE 

Application Requirements

Applicants must submit their application by email and provide the required materials in English.

The application should include:

1. CV

Applicants must submit an English-language CV highlighting their professional and media experience.

2. Letter of Intent

Applicants must provide a 500-word Letter of Intent in English.

The letter should describe the reporting beat they wish to cover.

Applicants should therefore clearly explain the area they want to specialise in and why it is relevant to their journalism career.

3. Two Story Pitches

Applicants must submit two story pitches in English.

These pitches should demonstrate the applicant’s ability to identify compelling stories and explain how they could be developed for an international audience.

4. Reporting Clips

Applicants may submit up to three clips of their reporting.

This component is optional, and the clips can be in Arabic.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply is:

Monday, August 24, 2026, at 5:00 PM Eastern Time (Toronto).

Applicants should ensure that their complete application reaches the programme before the stated deadline.

How to Apply

Applications should be submitted by email to:

Rob Steiner, Fellowship Director
University of Toronto

Email: robert.steiner@utoronto.ca

Applicants should also copy:

The Globe and Mail Foundation
Email: education@globeandmailfoundation.com

The application should contain the CV, Letter of Intent, two story pitches and, if available, up to three reporting clips.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Globe and Mail Foundation Scholarship for Syrian Media Professionals

Selection Process

Applications will be assessed by a volunteer jury.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their submissions clearly communicate their journalism experience, proposed reporting interests and ability to contribute to international media.

Particular attention should be given to the quality of the proposed reporting beat and story pitches, as these materials demonstrate the applicant’s ability to identify and develop stories.

Why This Fellowship Matters

The fellowship provides more than journalism training. It is designed to help a Syrian media professional develop the skills, professional relationships and confidence needed to work with international media.

Through mentorship and practical reporting, the selected Fellow can develop experience in:

  • International journalism
  • Investigative reporting
  • Story development
  • Story pitching
  • AI-assisted reporting
  • Freelance journalism
  • Professional newsroom engagement
  • Career development

The online format also means the selected Fellow can participate without being required to relocate to Canada.

Conclusion

The Globe and Mail Foundation Scholarship for a Syrian Media Professional is an opportunity for a Syrian media worker to strengthen their journalism career through the University of Toronto’s Dalla Lana Fellowship in Journalism and Health Impact.

Running from September 8, 2026, to March 16, 2027, the part-time programme combines journalism training, direct mentorship, story development, international reporting and professional career guidance. Participants can complete the fellowship entirely online, making physical relocation unnecessary.

Eligible Syrian media professionals with a strong working knowledge of English are encouraged to prepare their CV, 500-word Letter of Intent and two English-language story pitches before submitting their application.

item.content:encoded:
Emory University is inviting qualified candidates to apply for the Fellow Climate Solutions – Campus Services position within its Office of Sustainability Initiatives (OSI). The role offers an opportunity to contribute to university-wide climate and sustainability programmes, with a strong focus on student engagement, communications, events and sustainability initiatives.

The position is based at Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia, USA, and follows a hybrid work arrangement.

About the Climate Solutions Fellow Position

The Climate Solutions Fellow will serve for an initial one-year term, with the possibility of renewal for up to three years.

Working under the supervision of the Director of the Office of Sustainability Initiatives, the Fellow will support Emory’s sustainability vision by developing and coordinating programmes that engage students and the wider university community.

The role combines sustainability work with:

  • Student engagement
  • Event planning
  • Communications
  • Social media
  • Graphic design
  • Programme management
  • Relationship building
  • Campaign coordination
  • Sustainability education and outreach

The Fellow will work with graduate and undergraduate students across Emory’s nine Academic Units and collaborate with university committees, student organizations, interns and other campus groups.

Key Responsibilities

The successful candidate will contribute to a broad range of sustainability and student engagement activities.

1. Student Engagement

A major part of the position involves finding creative ways to engage Emory students in sustainability.

Responsibilities include:

  • Developing and implementing programmes for graduate and undergraduate students.
  • Building relationships with student organizations.
  • Working with student-facing university offices.
  • Responding to requests to participate in classes and student organization activities.
  • Speaking to classes and participating in campus events.
  • Supporting student engagement around Emory’s sustainability goals.

The Fellow will also help students become more involved in the university’s broader sustainability efforts.

2. Sustainability Events and Activities

The Fellow will help coordinate and participate in numerous campus activities.

These may include:

  • Weekly Farmers Market activities.
  • Wonderful Wednesdays tabling.
  • Student Sustainability Showcase and Forum.
  • Student orientation.
  • Sustainable Food Fair.
  • Earth Month activities.
  • Sustainability fairs and other campus events.

The Fellow may also represent the Office of Sustainability Initiatives at school-wide forums and sustainability committees.

3. Internship Programme Support

The Fellow will work with other OSI staff to support the administration and operation of the university’s sustainability internship programme.

This can involve:

  • Recruiting and hiring interns.
  • Onboarding interns.
  • Assigning tasks and activities.
  • Facilitating meetings.
  • Supporting interns throughout their programmes.
  • Carrying out other administrative and programme-related responsibilities.

4. Climate and Sustainability Strategy

The position contributes directly to Emory’s sustainability objectives.

The Fellow will support student engagement around key strategic plans, including the 2023 Climate Action Plan and Emory’s commitment to reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 50% by 2030 from a 2010 baseline.

This makes the role particularly relevant for candidates interested in climate action, sustainability strategy and environmental engagement.

5. Communications and Social Media

The position also has a strong communications component.

The Fellow will support OSI’s communications and marketing activities by:

  • Compiling the weekly newsletter.
  • Writing articles.
  • Developing social media content.
  • Creating digital communications materials.
  • Supporting report layouts and designs.
  • Developing graphics for sustainability communications.
  • Communicating campus-wide sustainability initiatives.

Candidates with social media and graphic design skills may therefore be particularly well suited to the position.

6. Relationship and Network Development

The Fellow will establish and maintain relationships with different groups both within and outside the university.

This includes working with:

  • Student sustainability organizations.
  • University departments.
  • Student-facing offices.
  • Campus committees.
  • Local organizations.
  • National groups.
  • Sustainability networks.

The Fellow will serve as a liaison between the Office of Sustainability Initiatives and various stakeholders.

APPLY HERE

Additional Duties

The position includes several additional areas of responsibility, including:

  • Event planning, management and execution.
  • Student engagement strategy.
  • Sustainability programme promotion.
  • Relationship and network development.
  • Digital communications.
  • Social media content creation.
  • Graphic development.
  • Campaign management.
  • Meeting coordination.
  • Identifying priorities and delegating action items.
  • Monitoring campaign outcomes.
  • Supporting OSI’s overall strategy and programme activities.

Minimum Qualifications

Applicants should meet the following minimum requirements:

  • A bachelor’s degree.
  • Some climate- or sustainability-related extracurricular, training, educational or internship experience.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Strong communication and outreach abilities.
  • Strong presentation skills.
  • Data management and analysis skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively.
  • Ability to work independently.

At least one year of professional work experience is preferred but is not listed as an absolute requirement.

Preferred Skills and Experience

Emory identifies several additional qualities that would strengthen an application.

These include:

  • Experience with campus sustainability initiatives.
  • Experience with climate action initiatives.
  • Demonstrated social media proficiency.
  • Graphic design experience.
  • Interest in learning additional software.
  • Experience working with students or student organizations.
  • Strong programme coordination skills.

Candidates who can combine sustainability knowledge with communication, digital media and student engagement skills may find the role particularly relevant.

Location and Work Arrangement

The position is based at:

Emory University – Clifton Corridor
Atlanta, Georgia, USA

The role is classified as Hybrid Remote.

The Fellow may work from home regularly but must be able to commute to Emory University on a flexible weekly schedule according to departmental needs.

Importantly, the position requires the successful candidate to reside in the state of Georgia.

Emory also reserves the right to change the remote-work arrangement with notice to the employee.

Equal Opportunity Employment

Emory University states that it is an equal opportunity employer.

Qualified applicants receive consideration for employment without discrimination based on characteristics protected under applicable state or federal law, including race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability and protected veteran status.

The university also states its commitment to providing reasonable accommodations and ensuring equal access for qualified individuals with disabilities.

Application Deadline

No application deadline is provided in the information supplied.

Applicants should therefore check the official Emory University job listing for the current closing date and application instructions before applying.

Visit HERE to learn about the Emory University Climate Solutions Fellow 2026

Conclusion

The Emory University Climate Solutions Fellow position offers an opportunity for a sustainability-focused professional to contribute to climate action, student engagement and sustainability programming within a major research university.

The role is particularly suited to candidates who have a bachelor’s degree and experience or training related to climate, sustainability, communications, social media, events or student engagement.

Because the position requires residency in Georgia and regular commuting to Emory University’s Atlanta campus, applicants should ensure they meet the location requirements before applying.

item.content:encoded:
The World Bank Institute for Economic Development offers a range of online learning opportunities designed to strengthen practical skills in areas such as data visualization, behavioural science, agricultural development, data management, and women’s economic empowerment.

These courses are delivered online and cover both technical and policy-focused topics. They can be useful for students, researchers, development professionals, government officials, economists, data professionals and other learners interested in building skills relevant to economic and social development.

Below are five courses, with each course highlighted separately alongside its respective course link.

1. Fundamentals of Data Visualization: Crafting Compelling Stories with Data

Delivery Mode: E-Learning
Location: Online
Language: English
Duration: 8 hours
Delivery Date Listed: March 31, 2026

The Fundamentals of Data Visualization course introduces learners to the principles of presenting data clearly and effectively.

The course focuses on the importance of data visualization as a communication tool and teaches participants how to select appropriate visualization methods depending on the type of data and communication objective.

What You Will Learn

Participants will learn how to:

  • Select the most suitable chart type for different datasets.
  • Understand the different components of a chart.
  • Apply best practices for creating clear and intuitive visualizations.
  • Turn complex questions and datasets into understandable visuals.
  • Create maps and infographics using Excel.
  • Improve the effectiveness of data-driven communication.

The course is particularly relevant for people who regularly work with data and need to communicate findings to decision-makers, colleagues, clients or the public.

Course Link

Enroll in Fundamentals of Data Visualization

2. Introduction to Behavioral Science in Public Policy

The Introduction to Behavioral Science in Public Policy course provides learners with an introduction to how behavioural science can influence the design and implementation of public policies.

The course explores how people think and make decisions and how behavioural factors can influence the effectiveness of government policies and programmes.

Areas Covered

The course looks at behavioural science applications in areas including:

  • Education
  • Healthcare
  • Social norms
  • Gender equality
  • Tax compliance
  • Climate change
  • Public policy

Participants are introduced to concepts involving automatic thinking, social influences and mental models. They also explore how cognitive biases can affect human behaviour and ultimately influence policy outcomes.

The World Bank describes the course as a prerequisite for accessing its full behavioural courses catalogue.

Course Details

Duration: 6 hours
Format: E-learning
Videos: 8 videos
Community: Multiple discussion forums

Course Link

Take the Introduction to Behavioral Science in Public Policy course

3. Using Evidence to Improve Jobs and Income in Agriculture

The Using Evidence to Improve Jobs and Income in Agriculture course provides practical guidance on using evidence to design better agricultural interventions.

The course forms part of the AgriConnect learning ecosystem, which provides a structured learning pathway from masterclasses to online courses and practitioner-led discussions.

It is based on the LEADS (Learn, Adapt, Scale) framework and focuses on translating research evidence into practical recommendations for agricultural development.

Key Areas Covered

Participants explore evidence and design considerations related to:

  • Agricultural extension systems
  • Input subsidies
  • Irrigation
  • Climate resilience
  • Market access
  • Agricultural interventions
  • Local adaptation of development programmes

The course also draws on the Development Economics Planet Lab toolkit, which brings together global evidence and translates it into actionable design principles.

Learners are encouraged to think critically about how agricultural interventions can be adapted to local contexts while maximizing impact and minimizing unintended distortions.

Course Details

Duration: 3 hours
Format: E-learning
Video Lessons: 5 videos
Certification: Free certificate upon completion

Course Link

Enroll in Using Evidence to Improve Jobs and Income in Agriculture

4. Documenting Development Data Using Metadata Standards

The Documenting Development Data Using Metadata Standards course focuses on improving the quality, discoverability and usability of development data.

The course is particularly relevant to people who produce, manage, curate or distribute datasets and want to ensure their data is properly documented and prepared for modern data applications, including artificial intelligence.

What the Course Covers

Participants learn how to create high-quality metadata that can:

  • Improve data discoverability.
  • Support data reuse.
  • Increase data credibility.
  • Improve data usability.
  • Support AI-readiness.
  • Ensure compliance with international metadata standards and best practices.

The course provides practical guidance on using a specialised Metadata Editor to create structured and standards-based metadata.

Who Can Benefit?

The course is designed for data producers and curators working in organisations such as:

  • Government agencies
  • International organisations
  • Academic data centres
  • Other institutions involved in collecting, managing and disseminating data

Course Details

Duration: 15 hours
Format: Self-paced e-learning
Videos: 7 hours
Certification: Certificate upon completion

Course Link

Enroll in Documenting Development Data Using Metadata Standards

5. Women, Business & the Law Online Course

The Women, Business & the Law Online Course examines how laws and legal restrictions can influence women’s economic opportunities around the world.

This self-paced course combines video lessons, expert insights and interactive assessments to help participants understand the legal barriers affecting women’s economic participation.

The course also focuses on how research and data can be translated into practical policy solutions that support women’s economic empowerment and economic growth.

Learning Objectives

By completing the course, participants can develop an understanding of:

  • Key legal constraints affecting women’s economic empowerment.
  • How to translate data and research into practical policy recommendations.
  • How to incorporate cross-country and regional data into policy work.
  • How research can be presented to decision-makers and ministers.
  • The relationship between women’s economic participation and economic growth.

Who the Course Is Looking For

The source specifically identifies the following groups:

  • Government officials
  • Technical staff from central banks
  • Secretariat and sectoral department staff
  • Officials from ministries of Economy and Finance
  • Officials from gender ministries
  • Social protection officials
  • Civil society organisations
  • Academics
  • Legal professionals
  • Economists

Course Link

Register for Women, Business & the Law Online Course

Why Consider These World Bank Online Courses?

Together, these five courses cover a broad range of skills that are increasingly important across development, government, research, economics and policy environments.

They provide opportunities to develop knowledge in:

  1. Data communication and visualization
  2. Behavioural science and policy design
  3. Evidence-based agricultural development
  4. Data documentation and AI readiness
  5. Women’s economic empowerment and law

Because the courses are delivered through e-learning, they can provide a flexible way for professionals and learners to develop additional skills alongside their existing studies or work.

Visit HERE to learn more about the World Bank Online Courses

Conclusion

The World Bank’s online learning opportunities provide training across several important areas of economic and social development. From learning how to communicate complex datasets through effective visualizations to understanding behavioural science, agricultural evidence, metadata standards and women’s economic empowerment, the courses cover both technical and policy-oriented skills.

Interested learners should review the individual course pages carefully for the latest enrolment information, course availability and any specific requirements before registering.

item.content:encoded:
The AI Safety Policy Entrepreneurship Fellowship (PEF) 2026–2027 offers an opportunity for early- to mid-career professionals who want to turn ideas about frontier artificial intelligence safety, security and governance into practical policy solutions.

Running from September 30, 2026, through February 28, 2027, the fellowship is designed around policy entrepreneurship rather than academic research alone. Fellows will work part-time as affiliates of the Federation of American Scientists (FAS), developing a concrete policy idea, engaging decision-makers, building coalitions and identifying realistic pathways for their proposal to influence policy.

The fellowship provides a $5,000 stipend, with an opportunity for an additional $1,000 merit award for the Fellow who develops the most specific and actionable policy memo and advocacy plan. Selected travel expenses for required in-person events are also supported through an additional travel stipend.

Applications must be submitted by 11:59 PM ET on September 7, 2026.

What Is the AI Safety Policy Entrepreneurship Fellowship?

The Policy Entrepreneurship Fellowship is an initiative designed to help participants move promising policy ideas beyond the conceptual stage and toward real-world implementation.

Rather than concentrating exclusively on producing research papers, the fellowship emphasizes the practical process of making policy happen.

Participants will be encouraged to:

  • Identify an important policy problem.
  • Develop a practical and implementable solution.
  • Identify institutions capable of implementing the solution.
  • Understand relevant decision-makers.
  • Engage policymakers and other stakeholders.
  • Build coalitions around their proposal.
  • Identify opportunities or “policy windows” for action.
  • Develop an advocacy strategy.
  • Produce a policy memo.
  • Move their idea toward practical policy adoption.

For the 2026–2027 cohort, the fellowship will specifically focus on frontier AI safety issues.

This makes the program particularly relevant to professionals interested in the intersection of artificial intelligence, public policy, national security, cybersecurity, governance, technology regulation and catastrophic risk management.

Fellowship Focus: Frontier AI Safety

The fellowship will explore policy challenges arising from increasingly capable and advanced AI systems.

Fellows are encouraged to examine different dimensions of frontier AI safety, including technical, regulatory, institutional and governance challenges.

Technical AI Safety

One area of focus is ensuring that frontier AI systems are:

  • Reliable.
  • Predictable.
  • Secure.
  • Aligned with human values.
  • Designed and deployed in ways that reduce serious risks.

Applicants with technical AI expertise may therefore be able to translate their technical knowledge into policy proposals addressing the governance of advanced AI systems.

AI Governance and Policy

Another major area involves developing frameworks for governing the development and use of frontier AI.

Potential questions may include:

  • What policies should govern advanced AI development?
  • Which institutions should oversee high-risk AI systems?
  • How should governments establish appropriate safeguards?
  • What regulatory mechanisms could reduce catastrophic AI risks?
  • How can governments build the capacity required to govern rapidly developing technologies?

Risk Assessment and Mitigation

Fellows may also explore ways to identify, evaluate and reduce risks associated with increasingly capable AI systems.

Potential policy approaches could involve:

  • Risk assessment frameworks.
  • Safety requirements.
  • Risk classification systems.
  • Governance mechanisms.
  • Monitoring and oversight.
  • Mitigation standards.
  • Institutional preparedness.

Transparency and Accountability

The fellowship also welcomes ideas addressing transparency and accountability in AI development and deployment.

This could include examining how governments, companies and other institutions can improve understanding of:

  • How advanced AI systems are developed.
  • What capabilities they possess.
  • What risks they create.
  • How they are deployed.
  • Who is responsible for managing those risks.
  • How oversight can be strengthened.

Priority Policy Themes

The fellowship is particularly interested in policy proposals addressing several emerging frontier AI safety and governance issues.

These include:

Cybersecurity

Applicants could examine cybersecurity risks associated with advanced AI systems and develop policy mechanisms designed to strengthen security.

Capability Thresholds

Another potential area is determining whether specific AI capabilities should trigger additional regulatory, safety or oversight requirements.

Risk Taxonomies

Fellows may explore systems for categorizing different types and levels of AI risk so that policymakers can develop proportionate responses.

Critical Infrastructure

Advanced AI could have implications for critical infrastructure and essential systems. Policy proposals could examine how these risks should be assessed and mitigated.

Compute Governance

Computational resources play an important role in the development of frontier AI. Fellows may explore governance mechanisms relating to access to, monitoring of or oversight of advanced computing resources.

Model Proliferation

The fellowship is interested in questions surrounding the proliferation of AI models, including the policy implications of open versus closed systems.

Policy Design and Government Capacity

Applicants may also propose broader approaches to policy design, institutional arrangements and government capacity for managing catastrophic risks associated with advanced AI.

What Is Expected From Fellows?

The fellowship is designed to give participants flexibility to pursue a policy project that they believe can create meaningful impact.

However, Fellows are expected to develop a concrete policy proposal rather than simply explore a broad research topic.

The central objective is to identify a specific frontier AI safety problem and develop a feasible pathway toward policy adoption.

Possible mechanisms for implementation could include:

  • Legislation.
  • Regulation.
  • Government standards.
  • Procurement requirements.
  • Institutional design.
  • Government policies.
  • Governance frameworks.
  • Other practical policy mechanisms.

Key Fellowship Deliverable: Policy Memo

One of the central responsibilities will be to develop and publish a policy memo addressing a specific frontier AI safety challenge.

The memo should go beyond describing the problem.

It should include:

  1. A clearly defined policy challenge.
  2. Evidence and analysis demonstrating why the issue matters.
  3. A practical policy solution.
  4. The institutions and decision-makers relevant to implementation.
  5. Key stakeholders who need to be engaged.
  6. A strategy for moving the proposal toward adoption.
  7. Consideration of practical barriers to implementation.

The goal is to produce a policy document that can contribute to an actual policy conversation.

Policy Entrepreneurship Training

Fellows will participate in training sessions designed to strengthen their ability to turn ideas into policy impact.

Training will address areas such as:

  • Frontier AI safety.
  • Policymaking processes.
  • Policy entrepreneurship.
  • Stakeholder engagement.
  • Translating technical expertise into policy.
  • Identifying policy opportunities.
  • Building coalitions.
  • Engaging decision-makers.
  • Moving policy proposals toward implementation.

Participants will also take part in reading groups intended to deepen their understanding of frontier AI safety and practical policymaking.

In-Person California Retreat

The fellowship includes an in-person California retreat tentatively scheduled for:

November 4–7, 2026

The retreat will focus on:

  • Mentorship.
  • Community building.
  • Developing fellowship projects.
  • Advancing policy proposals.
  • Connecting Fellows with relevant expertise and perspectives.

An additional travel stipend will be available to cover selected expenses associated with the California retreat.

Washington, DC Capstone Event

Fellows are also expected to participate in an in-person capstone event in Washington, DC, tentatively scheduled for the week of:

February 22, 2027

The capstone event is intended to provide an opportunity for Fellows to:

  • Launch their policy memos.
  • Disseminate their policy recommendations.
  • Engage policymakers.
  • Connect with experts.
  • Engage relevant stakeholders.
  • Present the outcomes of their fellowship projects.

This component gives Fellows an opportunity to move their work beyond the fellowship itself and into conversations with people involved in policymaking and governance.

Time Commitment

The fellowship is structured as a part-time opportunity.

Fellows are expected to dedicate an average of:

5 hours per week, or approximately 20 hours per month

to the fellowship during the period from September 30, 2026, through February 28, 2027.

This time commitment includes mandatory fellowship programming.

Participants will also take part in twice-monthly group check-ins.

FAS will make reasonable efforts to schedule these sessions at times that accommodate participants.

Select absences may be accommodated when participants provide appropriate notice, including absences related to:

  • Illness.
  • Work conflicts.
  • Vacation.

Exceptional circumstances may also be considered when determining whether a participant can be exempted from certain mandatory sessions.

Individual Mentorship

Each Fellow will receive individual support from FAS.

The fellowship includes:

  • Monthly individual check-ins with a dedicated FAS staff mentor.
  • Additional meetings when needed.
  • Additional communication and support as projects develop.
  • Assistance connecting Fellows with relevant experts and policy actors.

This mentorship component is particularly valuable for applicants who have strong technical or subject-matter expertise but limited experience navigating policy processes.

Fellowship Benefits

The AI Safety Policy Entrepreneurship Fellowship provides several professional and financial benefits.

$5,000 Fellowship Stipend

Each Fellow will receive a:

$5,000 stipend

This provides financial support for participants during the fellowship period.

Additional $1,000 Merit Award

An additional:

$1,000 merit award

may be provided to the Fellow whose policy memo and advocacy plan are judged to be the most specific and actionable.

This means that participants have an opportunity to receive up to $6,000 in total financial awards, excluding eligible travel support.

Travel Support

An additional travel stipend will help cover selected expenses associated with:

  • The California retreat.
  • The Washington, DC capstone event.

Professional Editing

Fellows will receive professional editing support for written products developed during the fellowship.

This can help improve the clarity, structure and professional quality of policy-related writing.

Policy Engagement Training

Participants will receive training from FAS staff focused on practical policy entrepreneurship.

This can help Fellows understand how to move from research and ideas toward policy influence.

Access to FAS Programming

Fellows will receive invitations to relevant FAS programming.

They will also have access to curated updates concerning the rapidly evolving federal science and technology policy landscape.

Deep-Dive Sessions

Participants will take part in interactive sessions examining practical aspects of policy entrepreneurship.

These sessions can help Fellows better understand how policy processes work in practice.

Expert Connections

FAS will support Fellows in connecting with relevant experts and policy actors.

This can help participants expand their professional networks and identify individuals and institutions that could contribute to their policy projects.

Who Is the Fellowship Designed For?

The fellowship is particularly well suited to early- to mid-career professionals who have strong subject-matter expertise but limited direct experience working in public policy.

The program is intended for people who want to learn how to translate their knowledge into practical policy impact.

Potential applicant backgrounds include:

  • Technical AI research.
  • Artificial intelligence.
  • Academia.
  • Think tanks.
  • Civil society.
  • Technology industry.
  • Law.
  • Cybersecurity.
  • National security.
  • Public policy.
  • Science and technology policy.
  • Related technical or policy disciplines.

The fellowship is not limited to people who have previously worked as professional policymakers.

In fact, candidates with substantial expertise in another field who want to learn how to translate that expertise into policy action may be particularly well suited to the program.

Selection Criteria

Applications will be assessed holistically.

The selection process will consider the overall strength of the applicant and their proposed policy project rather than relying on a single qualification.

1. Understanding of a Significant AI Safety Challenge

Applicants should demonstrate a clear understanding of an important frontier AI safety, security or governance problem.

The problem should be meaningful and sufficiently specific to support a practical policy intervention.

2. Concrete Policy Idea

Applicants should propose a concrete policy idea rather than simply identifying a broad concern about AI.

The proposal should be:

  • Specific.
  • Practical.
  • Implementation-oriented.
  • Connected to a real policy challenge.
  • Supported by a credible pathway toward adoption.

3. Understanding of Key Stakeholders

Applicants should consider which institutions, decision-makers and stakeholders would be necessary to implement their proposal.

This demonstrates that the applicant understands policy as a process involving multiple actors rather than simply producing a recommendation.

4. Understanding of Practical Policy Challenges

Strong candidates should recognize that good policy ideas can face significant implementation barriers.

Applicants should demonstrate willingness to think constructively about:

  • Political constraints.
  • Institutional limitations.
  • Stakeholder interests.
  • Implementation challenges.
  • Government capacity.
  • Competing priorities.
  • Practical pathways toward adoption.

5. Curiosity and Initiative

The fellowship seeks people who demonstrate curiosity, initiative and genuine interest in translating ideas into practical impact.

Applicants should demonstrate that they are prepared to take initiative rather than simply conduct research.

What Makes a Strong Application?

A competitive application should clearly connect problem, solution and implementation.

A strong proposal should answer questions such as:

  1. What specific frontier AI safety problem are you addressing?
  2. Why is this problem important?
  3. Who is affected by the problem?
  4. What policy intervention are you proposing?
  5. Which institution could implement it?
  6. Who are the relevant decision-makers?
  7. Which stakeholders would support or oppose it?
  8. What barriers could prevent implementation?
  9. How could those barriers be addressed?
  10. What practical opportunity exists for advancing the proposal?

The strongest applications are therefore likely to demonstrate not only knowledge of AI safety but also an understanding of how policy change actually occurs.

Why the Fellowship Is Valuable for AI Policy Careers

The rapid development of frontier AI is creating increasing demand for professionals who understand both technology and public policy.

However, technical expertise alone does not necessarily translate into policy influence.

This fellowship addresses that gap by helping participants develop the skills required to move from:

Technical or subject-matter expertise → Policy idea → Stakeholder engagement → Advocacy → Policy adoption

Participants can therefore develop capabilities in:

  • Policy analysis.
  • Policy writing.
  • Stakeholder mapping.
  • Coalition building.
  • Decision-maker engagement.
  • Advocacy strategy.
  • Policy communication.
  • Governance.
  • AI safety.
  • Science and technology policy.

For professionals considering long-term careers in AI governance, technology policy, national security, cybersecurity or public-interest technology, these capabilities can be particularly valuable.

Click HERE to read more.

Fellowship Timeline

The fellowship runs for approximately five months.

Fellowship begins: September 30, 2026

California retreat: November 4–7, 2026, tentatively

Washington, DC capstone: Week of February 22, 2027, tentatively

Fellowship concludes: February 28, 2027

Application deadline: September 7, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET

Application Deadline and Submission Requirements

Applications must be submitted by:

11:59 PM ET on September 7, 2026

Applicants should be aware that applications are accepted only through the designated application platform.

When applicants select the application link, they will be redirected to the relevant platform and will need to create an account in order to submit their application.

Candidates should therefore avoid waiting until the final hours to begin the application process.

APPLY NOW!

Important Application Considerations

Before applying, candidates should make sure their proposed project is sufficiently focused.

A broad proposal such as “AI safety should be improved” is unlikely to demonstrate the level of specificity expected from a policy entrepreneurship fellowship.

Instead, applicants should identify a concrete problem and explain how a particular policy mechanism could address it.

For example, a proposal might focus on:

  • A specific cybersecurity risk associated with frontier AI.
  • A governance mechanism for AI capability thresholds.
  • A framework for categorizing advanced AI risks.
  • AI risks to critical infrastructure.
  • Governance of computing resources.
  • Oversight of AI model proliferation.
  • Standards for high-risk AI systems.
  • Institutional capacity for managing catastrophic AI risks.

The proposal should then connect the problem to a realistic implementation pathway.

Conclusion

The AI Safety Policy Entrepreneurship Fellowship 2026–2027 offers an opportunity for professionals to develop practical solutions to some of the emerging governance challenges associated with frontier artificial intelligence.

The fellowship is particularly distinctive because it goes beyond traditional research. Participants are expected to identify a concrete policy problem, develop an actionable solution, understand the institutions and stakeholders involved, build relationships with decision-makers and pursue a realistic pathway toward implementation.

With a $5,000 stipend, potential $1,000 merit award, travel support, professional editing, policy training, mentorship and access to experts, the program provides both financial and professional support for participants seeking to develop careers at the intersection of AI safety and public policy.

Professionals from technical AI research, academia, cybersecurity, law, national security, civil society, industry, think tanks and related fields are encouraged to consider applying, particularly if they have a strong policy idea but limited direct experience navigating policymaking.

The application deadline is September 7, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET. Candidates should focus on presenting a specific frontier AI safety challenge, a credible policy solution and a practical strategy for moving that solution toward real-world adoption.

item.content:encoded:
Cyprus International University provides several forms of financial assistance to undergraduate students.

The university states that many students benefit from scholarships or discounted tuition fees, with awards commonly ranging from 50% to 100%.

The available opportunities include international student scholarships, academic scholarships, and athletic scholarships.

1. International Student Scholarship

One of the major opportunities for students coming from outside Cyprus is the International Student Scholarship.

According to CIU, all undergraduate international students are granted a 50% tuition fee scholarship.

This means eligible international undergraduate students can receive a substantial reduction in the amount they would otherwise pay in tuition fees.

The scholarship can make studying at CIU more financially accessible for students from different countries who are considering undergraduate education abroad.

Who is this scholarship for?

The international student scholarship is intended for:

  • International students.
  • Students applying for undergraduate programs at CIU.
  • Students who meet the university’s admission requirements.

The scholarship is particularly relevant for students looking for an international university experience while reducing their tuition costs.

2. Academic Scholarships

Prospective undergraduate students who have strong academic records can apply for an Academic Scholarship based on academic merit.

The scholarship ranges from:

50% to 100% off tuition fees.

The exact scholarship percentage depends on the applicant’s academic performance and the university’s assessment.

This means academically outstanding students may have the opportunity to receive a full tuition fee scholarship, while other eligible students may receive a partial tuition reduction.

Academic merit

Students applying for an academic scholarship should be prepared to demonstrate their academic achievements.

Depending on the university’s assessment and admission requirements, academic records may be important when determining eligibility for the scholarship.

Students with strong secondary-school results should therefore consider applying for the academic scholarship when submitting their application to CIU.

3. Athletic Scholarships

Cyprus International University also offers Athletic Scholarships to students with strong sporting backgrounds.

Prospective students can apply if they have evidence of sports performance at the national level.

The opportunity is also open to students who are:

  • Members of Supreme Sports Leagues.
  • Students who are expected to actively participate in a CIU sports team.
  • Prospective students who can demonstrate significant sporting achievements.

Applicants should be prepared to provide evidence of their sporting background and achievements.

This scholarship provides an opportunity for talented athletes to combine higher education with continued sporting development.

Scholarship Opportunities for Graduate Students

Cyprus International University also provides scholarship opportunities for students pursuing postgraduate education.

These opportunities are available to:

  • Master’s students.
  • PhD students.

Graduate students who meet the university’s academic requirements may apply for scholarship support.

Graduate Scholarship Eligibility

According to the stated requirements, CIU graduate students with a valid bachelor’s diploma and a Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of at least 3.50 may apply for a scholarship.

Therefore, applicants should have:

  • A recognized bachelor’s degree.
  • A minimum 3.50 CGPA.
  • Eligibility for the relevant Master’s or PhD program.
  • Any other admission requirements required by the university.

Students interested in postgraduate study should carefully review the requirements for their intended program because admission requirements can differ between academic disciplines.

What Do the Scholarships Cover?

The primary benefit described by CIU is a reduction in tuition fees.

Depending on the scholarship category, students may receive:

  • 50% tuition fee support.
  • 75% tuition fee support.
  • Up to 100% tuition fee support for qualifying academic scholarship recipients.

The exact scholarship percentage depends on the student’s category and eligibility.

Students should note that a tuition scholarship does not necessarily mean that every cost associated with studying abroad is covered.

Applicants should separately budget for expenses such as:

  • Accommodation.
  • Food.
  • Transportation.
  • Books and learning materials.
  • Visa-related expenses.
  • Health insurance where applicable.
  • Personal expenses.
  • Travel costs.

Students should confirm the current fee structure and exactly what their scholarship covers before making financial arrangements.

Progression Scholarships for Existing CIU Students

CIU also refers to progression scholarships for its students.

Students who are already studying at the university and want to learn more about progression scholarship opportunities are advised to contact the Registration Office.

The progression scholarship may be relevant to students continuing their studies and seeking information about scholarship opportunities based on their academic progress.

Since individual circumstances can vary, existing students should contact the Registration Office directly for the latest requirements and applicable scholarship rates.

How to Determine Which Scholarship You May Qualify For

Different students may be suited to different scholarship categories.

If you are an international undergraduate applicant

The International Student Scholarship may be particularly relevant because CIU states that all undergraduate international students receive a 50% tuition fee scholarship.

If you have excellent academic results

You may consider applying for the Academic Scholarship, which can provide between 50% and 100% tuition fee support based on academic merit.

If you are an accomplished athlete

The Athletic Scholarship may be appropriate if you have national-level sporting achievements, are a member of an eligible sports league, or intend to actively participate in a CIU sports team.

If you are pursuing a Master’s or PhD

Graduate scholarship opportunities are available for CIU graduate students who hold a valid bachelor’s diploma and have a minimum CGPA of 3.50.

Is There an Application Deadline?

No specific scholarship deadline is provided in the information supplied.

Students should therefore check the university’s current admissions and scholarship information before applying, as deadlines can vary according to the academic intake and program.

Applicants should avoid assuming that the absence of a stated deadline means applications can be submitted at any time. University admission periods and individual program deadlines may still apply.

Why Consider Cyprus International University Scholarships?

These scholarship opportunities can be attractive to students for several reasons.

Significant tuition reductions

Eligible students can receive tuition discounts ranging from 50% to 100%, depending on the scholarship category and academic performance.

Opportunities for international students

International undergraduate students are specifically supported through the university’s 50% tuition fee scholarship.

Support for academic excellence

Students with strong academic backgrounds can potentially qualify for scholarships covering up to 100% of tuition fees.

Opportunities for athletes

Students with significant sporting achievements can potentially combine their academic education with participation in university sports.

Postgraduate opportunities

Scholarship opportunities are also available for eligible Master’s and PhD students who meet the required academic criteria.

                     Learn more about this opportunity HERE

Tips for Prospective Applicants

Students interested in these scholarships should consider the following steps:

1. Identify the correct scholarship category

Determine whether you qualify through international student status, academic merit, athletic performance, or postgraduate academic qualifications.

2. Prepare academic documents

Applicants should have their relevant academic certificates, transcripts, and other educational documents ready.

3. Highlight your achievements

Students applying based on academic merit should clearly demonstrate their academic performance.

Athletes should prepare evidence of their sporting achievements, particularly national-level performance or membership in recognized leagues.

4. Check your postgraduate CGPA

Graduate applicants should ensure that they meet the stated minimum 3.50 CGPA requirement and possess a valid bachelor’s diploma.

5. Confirm current requirements

Scholarship rules, tuition fees, admission requirements, and payment procedures can change. Applicants should confirm the latest information with Cyprus International University before making final decisions.

                                                  APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The Cyprus International University Scholarship opportunities provide several pathways for students to reduce the cost of higher education. International undergraduate students are eligible for a 50% tuition fee scholarship, while academically strong students may apply for scholarships ranging from 50% to 100% of tuition fees.

Students with outstanding sporting achievements can also explore athletic scholarships, while eligible Master’s and PhD students with a valid bachelor’s diploma and at least a 3.50 CGPA can apply for graduate scholarship opportunities.

With options for international students, high-achieving students, athletes, and postgraduate students, CIU offers a variety of scholarship routes for those seeking to study in Cyprus.

Prospective applicants should carefully identify the scholarship category that matches their background, prepare the necessary academic or achievement documents, and confirm the latest admission, scholarship, tuition, and payment requirements directly with the university before applying.

Discover more global Scholarship opportunities on OFY HERE

item.content:encoded:
The Rideau Hall Foundation (RHF) is recruiting for multiple positions in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada, offering qualified professionals an opportunity to join an independent, non-partisan charitable organisation working across areas including learning, leadership, giving and innovation.

The current vacancies include positions in Programs, Partnerships, Philanthropy, Development and Executive Support, with opportunities available at different experience levels.

The three positions covered in this recruitment are:

  1. Coordinator, Programs and Partnerships – Full-time, permanent
  2. Manager, Corporate Philanthropy & Partnerships – Full-time, permanent
  3. Executive Assistant – Fixed-term, 14-month contract

All three positions are based in Ottawa, Ontario, under a hybrid work arrangement.

The roles offer competitive salaries and a range of employee benefits, including health and dental coverage, retirement savings programmes and paid vacation, depending on the position.

The Executive Assistant position has an application deadline of 14 August 2026, while the Manager, Corporate Philanthropy & Partnerships position closes on 24 August 2026. The Coordinator, Programs and Partnerships position will remain open until filled.

Rideau Hall Foundation Jobs 2026: Quick Overview

Position Employment Type Location Salary Range Deadline
Coordinator, Programs and Partnerships Full-time, Permanent Ottawa, Ontario, Hybrid $56,500–$61,000 Until filled
Manager, Corporate Philanthropy & Partnerships Full-time, Permanent Ottawa, Ontario, Hybrid $83,000–$95,000 24 August 2026
Executive Assistant Fixed-term, 14 months Ottawa, Ontario, Hybrid $67,000–$75,000 14 August 2026

Candidates for the positions must successfully pass all required security clearances.

About the Rideau Hall Foundation

The Rideau Hall Foundation (RHF) is an independent and non-partisan charitable organisation established to amplify the impact of the office of the Governor General as a central institution of Canadian democracy.

The organisation works to better serve Canadians through initiatives connected to:

  • Learning
  • Leadership
  • Giving
  • Innovation
  • Community development
  • Cross-sector partnerships

The Foundation works with partners across different sectors to celebrate excellence, create opportunities and connect communities with the broader objective of contributing to a better Canada.

Its work involves collaboration with organisations and stakeholders across Canada, making strong coordination, partnership development, relationship management and administrative skills particularly relevant to the available positions.

For more information, applicants can visit the official Rideau Hall Foundation website Here

1. Coordinator, Programs and Partnerships

Position Overview

The Coordinator, Programs and Partnerships is a full-time, permanent position based in Ottawa, Ontario, with a hybrid work arrangement.

The successful candidate will report to the Manager, Programs and Partnerships and will support the delivery of RHF initiatives across multiple portfolios and thematic areas, with a particular focus on the Innovation portfolio.

This position is suitable for a collaborative, organised and detail-oriented professional who is comfortable coordinating programmes, supporting partnerships, managing administrative processes and working with multiple stakeholders.

The role does not have supervisory responsibilities.

Position Details

  • Job title: Coordinator, Programs and Partnerships
  • Location: Ottawa, Ontario
  • Work arrangement: Hybrid
  • Employment: Full-time
  • Status: Permanent
  • Reports to: Manager, Programs and Partnerships
  • Supervisory responsibility: No
  • Posting date: 10 August 2026
  • Salary: $56,500–$61,000
  • Deadline: Until filled

About the Role

The Coordinator will play an important operational role in helping RHF deliver high-impact initiatives.

The successful candidate will support programme objectives through:

  • Programme coordination
  • Relationship management
  • Administrative support
  • Event coordination
  • Research
  • Communications
  • Database management
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • Digital content coordination

The position requires someone who can manage several responsibilities at the same time while maintaining accuracy, professionalism and effective communication.

Key Responsibilities

The Coordinator, Programs and Partnerships will be responsible for a broad range of duties.

Programme Coordination

The successful candidate will:

  • Coordinate, implement and track activities required for the smooth operation of multiple initiatives.
  • Support programme delivery and grant-making infrastructure.
  • Help develop plans and communication materials in collaboration with relevant RHF departments.
  • Support work planning and implementation.
  • Track programme activities and ensure important tasks are completed on time.

Events and Logistics

The position also involves coordinating both in-person and virtual events.

Responsibilities include:

  • Coordinating event logistics
  • Arranging travel
  • Supporting event communications
  • Working with partners
  • Following up after events
  • Ensuring appropriate materials are available

Internal Coordination

The Coordinator will work closely with RHF staff to ensure that important information is shared efficiently.

This includes distributing:

  • Meeting materials
  • Minutes
  • Reports
  • Relevant information
  • Opportunities
  • Other programme-related documents

Stakeholder and Partnership Support

The role includes identifying and supporting relationships with stakeholders.

The successful candidate may work with:

  • External specialists
  • Vendors
  • Programme partners
  • Other stakeholders

Effective relationship management and professional communication are therefore essential.

Research and Reporting

The Coordinator will also:

  • Conduct research
  • Write reports
  • Maintain databases
  • Maintain systems supporting RHF initiatives
  • Monitor programme information

Communications and Digital Content

Another important element of the position is communications support.

The successful candidate will work with the Communications department to coordinate the creation and management of digital content and campaigns across:

  • Social media
  • Websites
  • Newsletters
  • Other digital platforms

The role also involves supporting RHF’s brand messaging and monitoring engagement and performance metrics.

Information Booths and Promotional Materials

The Coordinator will organise RHF information booths at events and ensure that promotional and informational materials are:

  • Current
  • Accurate
  • Available
  • Suitable for print
  • Available in digital formats

Qualifications and Experience

Applicants should have:

  • A relevant diploma, or an equivalent combination of relevant training, education and experience.
  • At least 2 years of experience in programme and/or project management coordination.
  • Experience in administration.
  • Experience in project management.
  • Experience in event management.

Experience in the following areas is considered an asset:

  • Non-profit organisations
  • Charitable organisations
  • Small organisations
  • Start-up organisations
  • Start-up initiatives

Core Skills

Candidates should demonstrate the ability to:

  • Work effectively in a collaborative environment.
  • Work independently.
  • Demonstrate flexibility and initiative.
  • Manage competing priorities.
  • Find practical solutions to challenges.
  • Communicate professionally with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Understand social media and digital marketing.
  • Maintain excellent organisational and administrative standards.
  • Coordinate events effectively.
  • Navigate multiple team priorities.
  • Use software and CRM systems proficiently.

Salary and Benefits

The hiring range is $56,500 to $61,000, depending on experience and qualifications.

Benefits include:

  • Day-one access to extended health and dental coverage.
  • Employer-matched Retirement Savings Program.
  • Employee Assistance Program with 24/7 confidential support through TELUS Health.
  • 15 vacation days per year from the beginning of employment.
  • An additional five vacation days every three years, up to a maximum of 30 vacation days annually.

Application Deadline

The Coordinator position will remain open until filled.

Applicants are encouraged to apply as soon as possible because the vacancy may close once a suitable candidate has been selected.

                                       Read More And Apply HERE

2. Manager, Corporate Philanthropy & Partnerships

Position Overview

The Manager, Corporate Philanthropy & Partnerships is a full-time, permanent position based in Ottawa, Ontario, with a hybrid work arrangement.

This is a more senior role focused on developing and managing corporate relationships that support the Rideau Hall Foundation’s philanthropic and mission-driven priorities.

The successful candidate will report to the Director of Philanthropy and will be responsible for developing, managing and growing a national portfolio of corporate donors, sponsors and strategic partners.

Position Details

  • Job title: Manager, Corporate Philanthropy & Partnerships
  • Location: Ottawa, Ontario
  • Work arrangement: Hybrid
  • Employment: Full-time
  • Status: Permanent
  • Reports to: Director of Philanthropy
  • Supervisory responsibility: No
  • Posting date: 10 August 2026
  • Salary: $83,000–$95,000
  • Application deadline: 24 August 2026
  • Vacancy: One newly created position

About the Role

The Manager will play a central role in RHF’s fundraising and partnership development activities.

The position focuses on securing corporate philanthropic investments, sponsorships and strategic partnerships that support RHF’s mission and revenue objectives.

One of the major priorities connected to this position is Realize Ambition, RHF’s $250 million national campaign aimed at igniting Canadian ambition and contributing to a brighter future for Canadians.

The Manager will therefore need strong relationship-building, fundraising, business development and partnership management capabilities.

Key Responsibilities

Managing Corporate Partnerships

The Manager will:

  • Manage a national portfolio of corporate donors.
  • Manage corporate sponsors and prospective partners.
  • Develop strategic relationships.
  • Grow existing corporate partnerships.
  • Maintain long-term relationships with corporate stakeholders.

Prospect Development

The successful candidate will identify and qualify potential corporate partners and advance them through different stages of the partnership pipeline.

This includes:

  • Identifying prospects
  • Qualifying opportunities
  • Cultivating relationships
  • Soliciting support
  • Securing investments
  • Stewarding relationships
  • Renewing partnerships

Fundraising and Sponsorship

The Manager will seek to secure:

  • Philanthropic investments
  • Corporate sponsorships
  • Employee engagement opportunities
  • Partnership agreements

The position therefore requires demonstrated ability in corporate fundraising and partnership development.

Pipeline Management

The Manager will build and maintain a corporate opportunities pipeline with measurable:

  • Revenue targets
  • Engagement targets
  • Partnership opportunities
  • Relationship activities

Accurate records, forecasting and relationship information must be maintained within RHF’s CRM system.

Corporate Social Responsibility and ESG

The position will also involve identifying partnerships aligned with:

  • Corporate social responsibility
  • ESG
  • Community investment
  • RHF priorities

The Manager will monitor trends in corporate philanthropy, sponsorship, ESG and community investment and identify emerging opportunities.

Partnership Materials

The successful candidate will prepare materials such as:

  • Partnership proposals
  • Sponsorship packages
  • Presentations
  • Stewardship reports
  • Customised engagement opportunities

Strong written communication is therefore an important part of the role.

Campaign and Fundraising Planning

The Manager will contribute to:

  • Annual fundraising planning
  • Partnership planning
  • Budgeting
  • Forecasting
  • Reporting
  • National campaigns
  • Leadership giving initiatives

Qualifications and Experience

Applicants should have:

  • A post-secondary degree in a related field, or an equivalent combination of training and experience.
  • At least 5 years of experience in corporate fundraising, sponsorship, business development, partnerships or related relationship-management roles.
  • Demonstrated success securing and managing five- and six-figure corporate partnerships, sponsorships or philanthropic investments.
  • Experience managing complex pipelines.
  • Ability to advance multiple partnership opportunities simultaneously.
  • Working knowledge of CRM systems.
  • Knowledge of donor relationship management systems.
  • Understanding of moves-management strategies.
  • Experience with pipeline-management practices and tools.

Experience in a national charitable, public-sector, educational, cultural or social-impact organisation is also required as part of the preferred background.

Experience supporting:

  • National campaigns
  • Leadership giving initiatives
  • High-profile partnerships

is particularly relevant.

Familiarity with corporate ESG and community investment frameworks is also required.

Core Skills

The ideal candidate should demonstrate:

  • Strong corporate partnership management skills.
  • Strong sponsorship management skills.
  • Experience with philanthropic investments.
  • Excellent relationship-building abilities.
  • Networking skills.
  • Stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Strong proposal-writing skills.
  • Presentation skills.
  • Negotiation skills.
  • Stewardship skills.
  • Knowledge of the Canadian corporate philanthropy landscape.
  • Understanding of sponsorship.
  • Knowledge of ESG and community investment.
  • Strategic thinking.
  • Analytical skills.
  • Planning and execution skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
  • Ability to collaborate across departments.
  • Ability to engage senior stakeholders.
  • Professionalism.
  • Initiative.
  • Accountability.
  • Integrity.
  • Discretion.
  • Sound judgement.
  • Flexibility and adaptability.
  • Cultural awareness and sensitivity.

Salary and Benefits

The hiring range for the position is $83,000 to $95,000, depending on experience and qualifications.

The benefits package includes:

  • Extended health and dental coverage from day one.
  • Employer-matched retirement savings programme.
  • Employee Assistance Program with 24/7 confidential support.
  • 15 vacation days per year initially.
  • An additional five vacation days every three years, up to 30 days annually.

Application Deadline

Applications for the Manager, Corporate Philanthropy & Partnerships position must be submitted by:

24 August 2026

Applicants should ensure that their applications are submitted through the Rideau Hall Foundation career portal before the deadline.

 

3. Executive Assistant

Position Overview

The third vacancy is for an Executive Assistant supporting the Chief Impact Officer.

Unlike the first two positions, this role is a fixed-term position for 14 months.

The position is based in Ottawa, Ontario, under a hybrid work arrangement.

Calendar and Schedule Management

  • Adaptability.

  • Ability to work independently.
  • Ability to work collaboratively.

Strong English communication skills are required.

Applicants should also be highly proficient in:

  • Microsoft Excel
  • Microsoft PowerPoint
  • Microsoft Outlook

Salary and Benefits

Benefits include:

14 August 2026

Coordinator, Programs and Partnerships

$67,000–$75,000

With salaries ranging from $56,500 to $95,000, hybrid working arrangements and a range of employee benefits, these positions offer competitive opportunities within the Canadian charitable sector.
